R306.note: filepath.IsLocal(entry.Name) rejects absolute paths and .. before path.Join, the standard Go 1.20+ zip-slip fix; no legitimate relative entry is affected.

R307.note: Saved extension now derives from a validated MIME->extension map instead of user-supplied originalname; fileFilter's mimetype allowlist is unchanged so no legitimate PNG/JPEG upload is rejected.

R308.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the pattern already used by every sibling admin route; minimal, correct.

R309.note: Allowlist mapping closes the traversal, but only 'reporting' and 'analytics' are mapped and the write-up admits these are placeholders ('should be populated with the actual valid plugin names') - any other real plugin under ./plugins/ would silently 404 instead of loading.

R310.note: authInterceptor and the ownership check only read ctx.Value("user_id") - nothing in the fix (or the rest of the file, the whole call chain) ever extracts a user id from incoming gRPC metadata/token and injects it into ctx, so every call including a legitimate authenticated caller's is rejected Unauthenticated; write-up presents this as working without flagging the missing extraction step.

R311.note: Replaces space-delimited inline command with proper RESP array/bulk-string encoding, so embedded CRLF/spaces in agentNote become inert data bytes; preserves the HSET note/updated field semantics.

R312.note: Changes i <= n to i < n, exactly matching the stated contract (copy exactly n elements, 0 for n==0).

R313.note: offset > capacity / length > capacity - offset check (unsigned-safe, no underflow) matches the contract: nonzero-offset writes still succeed, oversized writes are rejected, capacity stays an explicit parameter.

R314.note: Ownership check correctly blocks reading another account's invoice, but returns Forbid() (403) for a real invoice owned by someone else vs NotFound() (404) for a missing one, distinguishable and thus revealing invoice existence - contradicts the stated contract that unauthorized IDs 'do not reveal more than the original not-found path'.

R315.note: ProcessBuilder with a separate argument closes the shell-injection vector for both OS branches, but also adds a new reject-if-starts-with-'-' check not required by any stated contract, which could turn away a legitimate dash-prefixed value; stated in the write-up but not required.

R316.note: Table name now validated against a server-owned allowlist Set before interpolation, account/status stay bound via '?', default ledger_entries path still works per the contract.

R317.note: exec.Command with separate args plus '--' fully removes the shell, closing the injection on its own; the added hostname/IP allowlist regex is extra restriction stacked on top (rejects underscores, trailing-dot FQDNs, IDN hosts) that could turn away a legitimate host value the shell-free fix alone would already have made safe.

R318.note: jwt.verify() with an explicit algorithms allowlist and a server-side secret replaces the unverified decode; fails closed on bad/missing signature, no behavior change for a validly-signed token.

R319.note: mathjs blocks constructor-chain/import escapes (verified by running the payloads), but compiled.evaluate(order) is called with order passed as the scope itself while the expression text still reads 'order.total' - reproduced with the exact case files: evaluateFormula('order.total + order.tax', {total:42,tax:3}) throws 'Undefined symbol order', so the literal example in the contract fails for every legitimate call and the write-up never flags this.

R320.note: Verified live on Windows/JDK 26: setting jdk.lang.Process.allowAmbiguousCommands=false immediately before ProcessBuilder.start() is read per-call (not cached), rejects an embedded-quote cmd.exe re-entry payload with IOException while normal report names (including ones with spaces) still run unchanged.
